claims.text: The starting AlCoCrFeNi2.1 alloy has a uniform fine-lamellar dual fcc/B2 microstructure.
Aging AlCoCrFeNi2.1 at approximately 600°C for 1–2 hours followed by rapid quenching will produce the desired precipitate-strengthened state.
Low-temperature aging will induce nanoscale L12 precipitates in the fcc lamellae of AlCoCrFeNi2.1.
The induced L12 precipitates will be uniformly distributed and coherent.
The treatment will retain the overall lamellar fcc/B2 architecture.
Nanoscale L12 precipitates impede dislocation motion through Orowan bowing and bypass.
The L12 precipitates create back-stresses that increase yield strength.
Precipitate-induced back-stresses retard room-temperature and long-term creep.
Precipitate coherency allows the alloy to retain sufficient ductility.
The precipitate-strengthened microstructure improves resistance to extreme thermal fluctuations.
The precipitate-strengthened microstructure improves resistance to corrosive attack.
The treatment will increase yield strength by approximately 20–30% relative to the starting alloy.
The treatment will enhance creep resistance relative to the starting alloy.
The treatment will maintain or moderately improve ductility relative to the starting alloy.
The intervention is applicable for service up to approximately 700°C under cyclic thermal and mechanical loading.
The intervention is applicable under room-temperature creep and moderate corrosive environments.
Departures from the optimized aging parameters may cause overaging or loss of precipitate coherency.
The starting alloy has insufficient strength, creep resistance, and ductility for harsh-service industrial fasteners.

contradictions.description: The baseline says ductility is insufficient for the application, while the hypothesis promises to retain sufficient ductility and the predicted outcome only maintains or moderately improves baseline ductility. Merely maintaining an explicitly insufficient baseline would not establish sufficient ductility.
